title: 2004 AMC 12B Problem 4
statement: An integer \(x,\) with \(10 \le x \le 99,\) is to be chosen. If all choices are equally likely, what is the probability that at least one digit of \(x\) is a \(7?\)

solutions.text:
There are \(90\) integers from \(10\) to \(99.\) Ten have a units digit \(7,\) and nine have a tens digit \(7.\) Since \(77\) is counted twice, there are \(10 + 9 - 1 = 18\) with at least one \(7.\) The probability is \(\dfrac{18}{90} = \dfrac{1}{5}.\)

Thus, the correct answer is B.
hints: Count two-digit numbers with a \(7\) in the units place and with a \(7\) in the tens place
\(77\) is counted in both groups, so subtract it once
